title: Phase-locked warmup capture notes (field scratch)
content:
Purpose:
- Explore phase-locked warmup as a deterministic way to reduce p99 during short bursts (10s–90s).
- Capture telemetry shape when we synchronize priming requests to worker epoch boundaries.

Environment:
- Model: local-quantized-v2 (8-bit, 16k context).
- Hardware: 1x A100-40GB isolated node (no co-tenants).
- Runtime flags: --continuous-batching=true --kv-cache-enabled=true --batch-size=32
- Harness: synthetic-arrival-generator v0.9 (zipfian alpha=1.2), sample clients = 120, duration per trial = 120s.

Experiment variants:
A) baseline: steady poisson arrivals, no explicit priming.
B) naive-priming: send N warmup tokens (10–50) immediately before real requests.
C) phase-locked: schedule warmup bursts that align with worker "epoch tick" (every 5s), ramped N across workers so overlap minimized.

Quick run summary (selected trials):
- Baseline (trial 2025-02-11T09:14): p50=38ms, p95=210ms, p99=720ms, throughput=870 req/s
- Naive-priming N=20 (2025-02-12T11:02): p50=45ms, p95=180ms, p99=560ms, throughput=820 req/s
- Phase-locked N=20 (2025-02-14T15:40): p50=40ms, p95=160ms, p99=320ms, throughput=840 req/s
- Phase-locked staggered (align+stagger across 4 worker groups) (2025-02-16T10:05): p50=41ms, p95=150ms, p99=290ms, throughput=830 req/s

Observations:
- Phase-locked consistently halved the p99 compared to baseline for short bursts: big win for UX-sensitive flows.
- Naive priming reduced cold-path work but caused throughput drop when many clients sent priming simultaneously (herd effect).
- Staggering across worker groups smoothed cache pressure and further improved tail.
- CPU on host spiked during priming windows (sys+io wait), suggests priming is shifted work rather than cheap no-op.
- KV-cache hit-ratio improved from ~0.21 baseline to ~0.64 with phase-locked priming (measured via runtime telemetry).

Micrograph (ASCII telemetry snapshot, phase-locked run):
time(s) | inflight | p99(ms)
0-5     | 30      | 280
5-10    | 90      | 320  <-- priming wave
10-20   | 45      | 150
20-60   | 12      | 110

Hypotheses / why it works:
- Aligning warmups to predictable ticks avoids random overlaps from independent clients, so KV cache warming becomes collective and amortized.
- Stagger reduces instantaneous kernel/context-switch pressure; CPU/PCIe contention fewer hot spikes.

Risks and caveats:
- Adds coordination complexity in real deployment (needs light-weight coordination endpoint or client timestamp heuristics).
- May be less effective under heavy multi-tenant noise or when worker topology changes (autoscaling).
- Could increase cost due to extra warmup tokens if not amortized across requests.

Next steps / action items:
- (A) Run multi-tenant variant: introduce 3 noisy tenants simulating 20% background traffic. Measure p99 drift.
- (B) Prototype cheap coordination: a stateless "phase beacon" header using broker TTL; test overhead.
- (C) Measure model memory pressure and PCIe utilization during priming; run perf counters.
- (D) Add experiment that primes only top-k tokens predicted by cheap prefix-model to reduce warmup token count.

Notes to self:
- Save full trace for best phase-locked run: /mnt/traces/phase-locked-20250214.tgz
- Talk to Arjun re: adding a small coordinator flag to the client SDK (linear INF-4123).
- Keep N small (<=40) when testing in shared infra to avoid destabilizing other experiments.

Conclusion (working):
Phase-locked warmup appears to be a practical mitigation for microbursts where p99 matters more than marginal cost. Next validation should focus on multi-tenant behavior and a low-friction coordination mechanism.
